notes:
- Sixteen people who had never seen Archie were written down as people, not as a feature list, and
  219 things they would really type were pushed through the product one at a time. Everything below
  is what that found. Eighty eight problems, all of them closed, and then a second pass by readers
  who had not been told what was fixed.
- Your agent knows it is shared. On an agent with more than one person on it, it was never told
  that, so "can Sam see this?" and "who else reads these?" were answered from a guess. It now knows
  who the owner is, who is speaking, and that the owner can read the conversation, and it says so
  when somebody asks.
- Everything your agent sends without being asked now goes to a chat you picked. Routine reports,
  reminders, watcher cards and morning briefings all went to whichever conversation happened to
  speak to it first, which on a shared agent could be a colleague's.
- Approving somebody from the waiting list now sends them a message. They were let in silently, so
  the first thing a new person heard from your agent was the answer to something they had asked
  before they were let in, and nobody ever told them the owner can read what they write.
- You can ask your agent whether a routine actually ran. "Did my morning brief go out?" and "has
  the pipeline report ever worked?" now have a real answer, including "it has never run", which is
  usually a computer that was asleep at the scheduled minute rather than anything broken.
- Switching a routine off by asking now switches it off. It reported success and kept firing until
  Archie was restarted.
- Removing a skill now takes its routines off the clock with it. They kept their schedule, fired
  every morning doing nothing, and stamped themselves as having run.
- A routine you add by asking for it keeps your time zone. It was set in UTC, so "every weekday at
  7" meant 2am for somebody in Chicago, and the confirmation never named the hour.
- A routine whose time passed while the computer was asleep is delivered late instead of thrown
  away, and a routine that is broken says so on the second failure rather than after two more weeks
  of its schedule.
- You can talk to your agent in the Archie window and be answered out loud. A voice note recorded
  there came back as a paragraph to read, while the same voice note sent from a chat app was
  answered in speech.
- A spoken "go ahead" now lands on the card you aimed it at. Recording a reply to a proposal
  reached your agent aimed at nothing, so the change you had just approved was already gone.
- A long spoken answer says why it came back in writing instead of going quiet, and a reply read
  aloud keeps the options in it. The one thing read out was the version with the choices stripped
  out, so somebody driving heard a question with no answers.
- "Read that back", "say that out loud" and every other way people ask for speech now work. It
  matched fourteen exact phrases and nothing else.
- You can say "send it" instead of tapping. On the chat apps that draw buttons, the words were
  switched off, which is exactly where somebody with their hands full needs them.
- A draft your agent scheduled for later cannot go out on its own without you asking for that time.
  The prompt promised nothing leaves without a press, and one setting had been quietly sending mail.
  A scheduled send now needs a person on the other end of the conversation and a time at least ten
  minutes out.
- A reply that failed to send is no longer left in the conversation as something your agent said it
  sent, and a failed delivery no longer destroys the reminder or the card it was delivering. Both
  go back on the list.
- Your records save out as a spreadsheet file. On the agent's page, under Records, there is an
  Export button that writes a CSV you can open in Excel or Sheets. The only way out before was
  asking your agent to retype the rows into the chat, which is slow, costs money by the row, and
  cuts off partway with nothing saying it did.
- Archie can tell you what removing it leaves behind, and where. Nothing in the product could say
  that your profile, memory, transcripts and job history stay on the disk after the app is gone.
- Your agent can say its own name. The name you gave it never reached the part that writes its
  replies.
- Ask "what did you do this week" and the answer comes from the record rather than from memory of
  the conversation. Two records existed and disagreed with each other.
- Every job on the Work board says who asked for it. Work a teammate requested was labeled "You
  asked" on the owner's board, and the name had been recorded for exactly that purpose and thrown
  away.
- A job that asked you a question in words stops sitting under "Needs you" forever. There was no
  card to press, so nothing could ever clear it.
- The store search finds add-ons by what you would call them. It could not see the trigger phrases
  every add-on is written to be found by, and answered a miss by saying the catalog cannot do it.
- An add-on your agent installs from chat works straight away. It was inert until Archie restarted,
  and the reply said it was ready.
- Add-ons that cannot install are no longer offered. The offers reached the model with every
  requirement stripped off them.
- A skill you write yourself with a blank "One line" is no longer invisible. Every screen said it
  was installed and working while nothing could route to it.
- The skill editor names the tools you can use, and says which field decides when your skill runs.
  It asked you to name tools and listed none.
- A reminder set by voice arrives out loud. It was delivered silently while the description your
  agent wrote its promise from said it would speak.
- A reminder Archie set for you off the back of a text says so, and names the switch that turns it
  off. It appeared in your list with nothing to say where it came from.
- Times are written the way you would say them, on a 12-hour clock, including the read-back whose
  whole job is to let you catch a wrong hour.
- Your agent's memory is honest about what it holds. A background pass was writing durable notes
  about you with no tool call, no record and no sentence in any reply, and one standing instruction
  told it not to say it did not know.
- Undo covers the whole turn. Several deletes in one turn shared one undo slot, so it restored one
  row and your agent confirmed everything was back.
- Fixed: a turn that died left "Working on it" in the thread forever. It now owns up to it on the
  next start.
- Fixed: a delivered text could report itself as failed and invite you to send a second copy.
- Fixed: undoing a filed email did nothing on Outlook. It worked on Gmail only, and said nothing.
- Fixed: a guest could tick the owner's task off, or settle the owner's card, by typing a number
  instead of tapping.
- Fixed: a guest's words could be written into the owner's permanent memory.
- Fixed: on a shared agent, a group room could be adopted as "the owner's own conversation", which
  put everything the product keeps out of rooms into one.
- Fixed: every check that keeps a room out of the delivery chat was inert on Discord.
- Fixed: `/invite` on an agent that only talks in the Archie window minted codes nobody could
  redeem, and told the owner to hand them out.
- Fixed: clearing a conversation was open to anybody in it, so a guest could wipe the room's thread
  for everyone.
- Fixed: connecting a company mailbox gave your agent no mail ability at all, and nothing said a
  skill was also needed.
- Fixed: the read-only calendar note and two other connect sentences were written to the owner and
  read out to guests word for word.
- Fixed: a table asked for in the Archie window rendered as literal pipe characters.
- Fixed: a stopped agent drew no Start button once there was a conversation on screen.
- Fixed: two evening journal routines fired half an hour apart on every new agent, one of them the
  add-on written to replace the other.
- Fixed: the alarm for a hand-written skill naming a tool that does not exist was sent to us and
  never to the person who wrote the skill.
- Fixed: a records query that matched nothing looked exactly like a list that is empty, and a query
  capped at fifty rows read as the whole list.
- Fixed: a document read from your knowledge base reached the model with nothing marking it as
  something a stranger wrote.
- Fixed: every turn told your agent its voice had just changed, on agents whose voice never had.
- Fixed: the first-run interview swallowed every message you sent, including requests, and had no
  way out from a phone.
- Fixed: your agent was told it could not do things that were on its own tool belt, and told to
  point at instructions that were not there.
